territorial_scope.description: Applies to U.S. persons' covered data transactions with countries of concern and covered persons, including persons designated as covered persons under subpart G.

evidence.quote: The rule (1) identifies certain classes of highly sensitive transactions with countries of concern or covered persons that the rule prohibits in their entirety

summary.short: US Department of Justice final rule (28 CFR Part 202), effective April 8, 2025, implementing Executive Order 14117. It prohibits or restricts U.S. persons' data brokerage, vendor, employment and investment transactions giving countries of concern or covered persons access to bulk sensitive personal or government-related data.
summary.long: Final rule of the U.S. Department of Justice, National Security Division, 28 CFR Part 202, effective April 8, 2025, implementing Executive Order 14117 of February 28, 2024. It concerns U.S. persons' covered data transactions that give countries of concern or covered persons access to government-related data or bulk U.S. sensitive personal data. Subpart C prohibits data brokerage and related transactions, including certain human 'omic data transactions and evasions. Subpart D authorizes restricted transactions (vendor, employment and investment agreements) only if CISA-based security requirements are met. Definitions cover sensitive personal data categories (covered personal identifiers, precise geolocation, biometric identifiers, human 'omic, personal health and personal financial data), bulk thresholds (for example 100 U.S. persons for human genomic data), countries of concern (subpart F) and covered persons, including designation (subpart G). Subpart E sets exemptions, such as official U.S. Government business, financial services and regulatory approval data. Subpart H provides for licenses, subpart I for advisory opinions, subpart J for due diligence and audits (certain provisions applicable from October 6, 2025), subpart K for recordkeeping and reporting, and subpart M for penalties and findings of violation.

notes: Part 1 of 5 covers the front matter, the Executive Summary, Background, Rulemaking Process, and Part IV discussion through section 202.205. It contains no codified operative provisions, so no obligations, thresholds, enforcement, events or definitions are coded here. Relations and entities come only from this part. target_instrument_id is empty because no registry IDs were provided for the targets. Internal inconsistency: the NPRM comment period is described as 30 days (fn. 32) and as 31 days (Part III). DATES gives an effective date of April 8, 2025, and the preamble says compliance for subpart J and §§ 202.1103–202.1104 is delayed to October 6, 2025; these dates belong to later parts' events. Lei and ticker are not verified and are left empty. Part 2 of 5 is Federal Register preamble text (responses to public comments on Sections 202.205 to 202.511), not operative regulatory text. It therefore yields relations and entities only; obligations, thresholds, events, enforcement and definitions in the cited sections belong to the parts that contain them. The preamble states that the Department 'declines to adopt' several requested changes; these are noted as preamble positions, not as rule text. The 'lotter on DSK' and page-header artifacts in the source are extraction noise. The Order is not identified by number in this part. This part (3 of 5) covers Federal Register preamble commentary (pp. 1685 to 1706) and the regulatory text §§ 202.101 to 202.106 and definitions §§ 202.201 to 202.213 (through Cuba). Only relations, entities and notes are populated here; other sections are annotated in other parts. Internal point to check against the later part containing § 202.1104: § 202.102(c) counts days as calendar days, while the preamble describes the NPRM reporting period for rejected transactions as '14 business days' and elsewhere as a '14-day period'. Preamble cost, burden and penalty figures are not coded here. This is part 4 of 5: §§ 202.214 to 202.259 (definitions, with examples) and subparts C to M (§§ 202.301 to 202.1306). Obligations, thresholds, enforcement and dates are in other parts or not coded here. Subpart N (Government-Related Location Data List) is headed in this part but its content is not reproduced in this extract. Countries of concern listed in § 202.601(a) and the Covered Persons List are not coded as entities. Relations and entities are populated above; the target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry IDs were supplied. section_status entries below are included only because the schema requires them. Part 5 of 5 contains only the Data List: Table 1 to § 202.1401 (Government-Related Location), giving latitude/longitude corner pairs for geofenced areas by Area ID. It contains no operative obligations, thresholds, definitions, enforcement provisions, relations or designations. In the source the minus sign appears as the character '¥' and coordinate pairs often wrap across lines and page breaks; values are not normalised here. The signature block names the signing official (Assistant Attorney General for National Security, U.S. Department of Justice) and the date December 26, 2024, but assigns no designation or role.
